# Kit index: one line per catalogue row

*Generated by `kit/build.py` from `kit/index.jsonl`; do not edit by hand. The Rule 30 Prize kit at commit `6289b3b`
(main, 2026-11-28): every table row of `lean/README.md` (328) and `equivalents/README.md` (106), condensed. Each line:
module, date added, contributors, weight, what is proved, and the open statements it defines or uses with the
implications it proves. Weight 3 = a reduction between open statements, a new open statement, a barrier, or an
exclusion of an infinite family; 2 = a substantial theorem; 1 = corollaries, extensions, tooling and certificate
data. Almost every row added after 20 October also carries extensions by G.P.J.W. Quint with Gemini; that credit
is omitted. A module listed in two catalogue tables has two lines, tagged with the table. The concise map is
[KIT.md](KIT.md); [KIT-UPDATE.md](KIT-UPDATE.md) keeps both in step with the kit. Verify against the kit before citing.*

## The statements (3)

- **Rule30Coupled** · 2026-10-17 · kit · W3. In any configuration the two halves evolve as halves driven by the centre column, centre updated from its driven neighbours; conversely gluing works (`evol_glue`). CQ ω ⇔ no finite configuration has centre ω (`CQ_iff_no_finite_config`); the family implies Problem 1. Ext: CQ phase-shift invariance; constant columns; driven neighbours aperiodic; Problem1 reductions to half-balanced even periods. *Open/implications:* CQ ω (open for every nonconstant periodic ω) ⇔ no finite configuration has centre column ω; FinConf for one column ⇔ CQ ω for all periodic ω with a black cell; that family ⇒ Problem1; CQ altCol ⇔ CQ01. Ext, each ⇒ Problem1: CQ for nonconstant periodic ω with ω 0 = true; Problem2 + CQ on canonical half-balanced even-period columns; Problem2 + CQ01 + CQ on half-balanced even periods 2m ≥ 4; Problem2 + CQ01 + CQ w0011Col + CQ on half-balanced even periods 2m ≥ 6; HalfDensity (subseq center 2 r) + Problem2 + CQ w0011Col + CQ on half-balanced periods 4k ≥ 8 (no CQ01); HalfDensity along strides 2^a (1 ≤ a ≤ K) + Problem2 + CQ on periods 2^(K+1)·q; modulo-8 version on periods 8q ≥ 8 (no CQ01, no CQ w0011Col). Also stride-4 HalfDensity + CQ w00001111Col + CQ w00101101Col ⇒ period-8 coupled discharge
- **Rule30Problem3** · 2026-10-24 · kit · W3. Prize Problem 3 on a one-tape Turing machine reading the binary digits of n: formal (no machine computes c(n) in time O(n)), verbal (o(n)) and model-independent (n^o(1)) versions, each implying the next (`problem3Verbal_of_problem3`, `problem3Robust_of_problem3Verbal`). Ext: output uniqueness, halting-time bounds, negation closure, bounded-time and 1-step centre exclusion, causal-speed bounds. *Open/implications:* Problem3 ⇒ Problem3Verbal ⇒ Problem3Robust
- **Rule30Prize** · start · kit · W3. States Problems 1 and 2 as in formal-conjectures' Other/Rule30.lean. Proves no column is eventually constant, so period 1 is excluded for every column and every transient. `no_column_eventually_constant`, `center_not_eventually_period_one` *Open/implications:* Problem1, Problem2 (stated, open)

## Period 1 and constant runs (4)

- **Rule30CenterRuns** · 2026-10-24 · Perez Morales (Claude Fable 5.1) · W3. Centre-column block of L equal cells starting at time a≥1: L≤a if black (`black_run_le`), L≤a-1 if white, L≤a-3 for white with a≥3 (`white_run_le_three`). Hence both colours in every window [a,2a]; log2 n ≤ blackCount n; m white cells before 4^m. Ext: blackCount + whiteCount = n; two-sided logarithmic bounds; FinConfig black-run bound.
- **Rule30SettledBarrierEffective** · 2026-10-27 · @AIOvernight (OpenAI Codex, Claude) · W2. Every black run of the single-seed centre, length L from a≥16, has 5L+3·log2(log2 a) ≤ 3a+21; every white run from a≥256 has L+log2(log2 a) ≤ a+2, floor logarithms (`black_run_loglog`, `white_run_loglog`). Ext: sub-linear windows with both centre colours and a transition; column −1 black-cell forcing.
- **Rule30BlackRunErosion** · 2026-10-28 · @AIOvernight (OpenAI Codex, Claude) · W2. Backward erosion of alternating spatial blocks: each black centre run of length L starting at a≥1 has L+2⌊(a−1)/5⌋≤a (`black_run_le_erosion`; Goux's bound R30-20261025-0554f7, separate formalization), plus a white-run erosion bound (`white_run_le_erosion`). Ext: sharp L+2(a/5)≤a for all a; parity-resolved D0/D1 boundary collisions; parity-sharpened white-run erosion.
- **Rule30SettledBarrier** · 2026-10-28 · @AIOvernight (OpenAI Codex, Claude) · W2. Settled white left diagonals obstruct long constant centre runs: for every additive margin M, 5L+M≤3a for black runs and L+M≤a for white runs at all sufficiently large starting times a (`black_run_margin_unbounded`, `white_run_margin_unbounded`). Ext: a single settled pair (k, k+2) gives L+k ≤ a+2; generalized constant-diagonal barriers.

So the degree is n for odd n and n - 1 for even n (`check_degree`), and ones n ≡ n mod 2 (`ones_parity`). Ext: the other phase has full degree and is never balanced.
- **Rule30ConeTip** · 2026-11-10 · Herbert (Claude, GPT) · W2. For every t ≥ 2 and every row L, the second difference of zrow L t 1 in depths t - 1 and t is t - 1 mod 2, the same on every row (`cone_tip`). For even t, every function with vanishing second differences there, in particular every affine one, misses the tip on each four-row face (`face_disagree`), so the tip is not affine (`tip_not_affine`).

## Equivalent forms and sufficient conditions (`equivalents/`, 106 modules)

### Proved equivalent to Problem 1 (47)

- **BinaryIrrational** (real numbers). x₂ = 0.c(0)c(1)… is irrational in base 2, base 10 or any base B ≥ 2; in a real base β > 2 the value is one-to-one. `problem1_iff_irrational_binary`, `problem1_iff_irrational_base`
- **NumberTheory** (number theory). The continued fraction of x₂ does not terminate; infinitely many approximations with error < 1/q²; `LiouvilleWith 2 x₂`; infinite order and dense multiples on the circle; x₂ not doubling-preperiodic; no long division p/q gives the digits. `problem1_iff_cf_not_terminates`, `problem1_iff_dirichlet` (P2: `problem2_iff_doubling`)
- **TwoAdic** (number theory). The 2-adic number Σ c(t)2ᵗ is irrational; a congruence form for every base p ≥ 2; 2-adic (FCSR) complexity unbounded. `problem1_iff_padic_irrational`, `problem1_iff_padic_int`, `problem1_iff_two_adic_complexity`
- **PowerSeriesF2** (algebra). Σ c(t)Xᵗ is not rational over F₂; no LFSR generates c; linear complexity unbounded. `problem1_iff_series_not_rational`, `problem1_iff_no_lfsr`, `problem1_iff_linear_complexity_unbounded`
- **LinearRelations** (algebra). Over any field: series not rational, no linear recurrence; shifts of c linearly independent; Hankel rank unbounded; Kronecker determinant criterion over ℤ, F₂, any field. `problem1_iff_shifts_linearIndependent`, `problem1_iff_hankel_rank_unbounded`, `problem1_iff_hankel_det_int`
- **ShiftOrbit** (combinatorics on words). The shift orbit of c is infinite; c is not preperiodic; Morse–Hedlund: at least n + 1 distinct blocks of every length n. `problem1_iff_infinite_shifts`, `problem1_iff_ncard_factors`, `problem1_iff_strictMono_ncard_factors`
- **WordsAutomata** (combinatorics on words). No word repeats forever; right-special block of every length; tail complexity ≥ n + 1; ω-limit set infinite; finite-state predictors err infinitely often; no feedback shift register; max-order complexity → ∞ ([28]). `problem1_iff_no_eventual_word`, `problem1_iff_unpredictable`, `problem1_iff_maxOrderComplexity_tendsto`
- **TransformsSeeds** (combinatorics on words). The same for shifts, XOR derivative, running parity and decimations of c; the Π₂ form; factorial periods; the formal-conjectures statement and Wolfram's 2019 statement (intended reading; the literal one is degenerate); every stripe seed 1, 11, 101, 1011, … has column c. `problem1_iff_xor_derivative`, `problem1_iff_decimation`, `problem1_iff_fc`, `problem1_iff_wolfram`, `problem1_iff_stripeSeed`
- **IntegerRows** (number theory). a(0) = 1, a(t+1) = a(t) XOR (2a(t) OR 4a(t)) (A110240): bit t of a(t) is not eventually periodic (EP); same for the diagonal of the bit array; row j has period dividing 2^j. `problem1_iff_integer_rows`, `problem1_iff_diagArray`, `diagArray_row_periodic`
- **TFunction** (algebra). Bit t of Φᵗ(1) is not EP, Φ(x) = x XOR (2x OR 4x); Φ permutes ℤ/2ⁿ and Φ^(2^j) is the identity mod 2^(j+1). `problem1_iff_orbit`, `orbit_two_pow_mod`, `testBit_orbit`
- **AutomatonGroup** (automata). Bit t − 1 of aᵗ(0), a(y) = y ⊕ (2y ∨ 4y ∨ 3) (black-wall column), is not EP ([54]); the transducer generates automaton group 2369; Φⁿ σ Φ⁻ⁿ has depth exactly 2n + 1. `PhiS_one`, `conj_finitary`, `conj_sigma_depth` (the equivalence itself, `problem1_iff_black_wall`, is in CATALOG/Lean, not this row)
- **LogicAutomata** (logic/computability). The black times are not Presburger-definable (any parameters) and not semilinear; {1ⁿ : c(n) = 1} and the prefix language of c are not regular. `problem1_iff_not_presburger`, `problem1_iff_not_semilinear`, `problem1_iff_unary_not_regular`, `problem1_iff_prefixes_not_regular`
- **Realization** (dynamics). No EP column is realized by the single seed (inverse problem); `Real.ofDigits` of c is irrational in every base; so is `cantorFunction (1/b) c`; Jen: `problem1_iff_column_iff_both`. `problem1_iff_realization`, `problem1_iff_irrational_ofDigits`
- **MonadicLogic** (logic/computability). The black times are not MSO-definable over (ℕ, <) ([36]), by the composition method with k-types, without automata. `problem1_iff_not_msoDefinable`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_msoDefinable`
- **OmegaRegular** (automata). No Büchi automaton accepts exactly c: {c} is not ω-regular. `problem1_iff_not_omega_regular`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_omegaRegular_singleton`
- **Holonomic** (algebra). c satisfies no recurrence Σ pᵢ(n)·c(n+i) = 0 from any point on, with polynomial coefficients not all zero (not P-recursive). `problem1_iff_not_pRecursive`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_pRecursive`
- **DFinite** (algebra). Σ c(t)Xᵗ is not D-finite over ℚ(X): no Σ qᵢ(X)·F⁽ⁱ⁾ = 0 with polynomial coefficients not all zero. `problem1_iff_not_dFinite`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_dFinite`
- **TailLanguage** (combinatorics on words). The number of words occurring infinitely often is strictly increasing in length; no tail Rauzy graph is a single cycle; the two-sided tail subshift is infinite. `problem1_iff_tail_strictMono`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_tail_flat`, `problem1_iff_tailSubshift_infinite`
- **CoupledHalves** (dynamics). No solution of the causal system u(t+1) = rule(left half driven by u at −1, u(t), right half driven by u at 1), u(0) = 1, is EP; its only solution is c. `problem1_iff_coupled_halves`, `eq_center_of_solves`
- **LempelZiv** (combinatorics on words). The Lempel–Ziv (1976) complexity of the prefixes of c is unbounded. `problem1_iff_lz_unbounded`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_lz_bounded`
- **Automatic** (automata). Automatic complexity of the prefixes → ∞ (no K-state DFA uniquely accepts infinitely many prefixes). Sufficient: not k-automatic for some k ≥ 2, or not both 2- and 3-automatic. `problem1_iff_automaticComplexity_tendsto_top`, `problem1_of_not_two_three_automatic`
- **PisotNumbers** (number theory). Σ c(t)·β^−(t+1) ∉ ℚ(β) for every Pisot β > 2 (Schmidt, 0/1 digits); sufficient direction for any base β > 2. `problem1_iff_not_mem_adjoin`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_mem_adjoin`, `problem1_of_not_mem_adjoin`
- **PisotBase** (number theory). β = 1 + √2: the value is not a + b√2 with a, b rational. `problem1_iff_not_mem_Q_sqrt_two`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_mem_qsqrt2`, `isPisot_β`
- **Expansions** (real numbers). The Engel, Sylvester (greedy Egyptian) and factorial-base expansions of x₂ are infinite; no k!·x₂ is an integer; the Lüroth expansion is not EP. `problem1_iff_engel_infinite`, `problem1_iff_sylvester_infinite`, `problem1_iff_luroth_not_eventuallyPeriodic`
- **WordForms** (combinatorics on words). Finite prefix certificates (> N factors of one length); black gaps, white gaps and run lengths not EP; unbordered factors ([51]); prefixes with no φ²-power ([47]); return words. Sufficient: unbounded LZ. `problem1_iff_prefix_certificates`, `problem1_iff_black_gaps`, `problem1_of_lz_unbounded`
- **Lagrange** (real numbers). θ = [1 + c(0); 1 + c(1), 1 + c(2), …] is not a quadratic irrational ([39]), through Euler–Lagrange. `problem1_iff_not_quadratic`, `digit_periodic_iff`, `quadratic_cfValue_iff`
- **Minkowski** (real numbers). y = [0; 1, r₁, r₂, …] (r_k the run lengths of c), equal to ?⁻¹(x₂), is not a quadratic irrational ([49]); Denjoy ?(y) = x₂ proved. `problem1_iff_minkowski_not_quadratic`, `questionMark_yMink`
- **ContextFree** (formal languages). {1ⁿ : c(n) = 1} and the prefix language of c are not context-free ([40]); pumping lemma for every grammar; regular ⟹ context-free. `problem1_iff_unary_not_contextFree`, `problem1_iff_prefixes_not_contextFree`, `pumping`
- **AlgebraicDFinite** (algebra). Σ c(t)Xᵗ is transcendental over ℚ(X) ([38]); in characteristic 0, algebraic over K[X] ⟹ D-finite, so [31] applies; Fatou not needed. `problem1_iff_transcendental`, `exists_dfinite_of_isAlgebraic`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_isAlgebraic`
- **SkolemMahlerLech** (algebra). The black times are not the zero set of any linear recurrence sequence over ℚ ([45]); Skolem–Mahler–Lech proved the p-adic way. `problem1_iff_not_LRS_zero_set`, `skolem_mahler_lech`, `epSet_zeros_matrix`
- **DiophantineGraph** (logic/computability). The graph of c is Diophantine (Lucas mod 2, half adder, history in blocks of width 2n + 4), so Problem 1 is a ∀∃ sentence about one polynomial equation. `center_diophFn`, `problem1_iff_forall_exists_poly`, `center_iff`
- **Cobham** (automata). c is not both 2- and 3-automatic; c is not k-automatic for some k ≥ 2 ([42]); Cobham's theorem for multiplicatively independent bases (Krebs). `problem1_iff_not_two_three_automatic`, `problem1_iff_exists_not_automatic`, `eventuallyPeriodic_of_isAutomatic`
- **Christol** (algebra). Σ c(t)Xᵗ is transcendental over F₂(X) or over F₃(X) ([42]); Christol's theorem for every prime p. `problem1_iff_transcendental_F2_or_F3`, `isAutomatic_iff_isAlgebraic`, `not_isAutomatic_iff_transcendental`
- **BuchiArithmetic** (logic/computability). The black times are not definable both in (ℕ, +, V₂) and in (ℕ, +, V₃) ([42]); (ℕ, +, V_k)-definable ⟹ k-automatic. `problem1_iff_not_buchi_definable`, `isAutomatic_of_definable`, `eventuallyPeriodic_of_definable`
- **OneTapeGap** (logic/computability). No one-tape Turing machine decides {1ⁿ : c(n) = 1} in time o(n log n) ([43], time); Hennie's theorem for unary input. `problem1_iff_no_fast_one_tape_decider`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_exists_fast_decider`
- **OfflineGap** (logic/computability). No read-only-input TM decides {1ⁿ : c(n) = 1} in space o(log log n) ([43], space); with Cobham, no such machines from both the base-2 and base-3 digits of n. `problem1_iff_no_small_space_decider`, `problem1_iff_no_small_space_digit_deciders`
- **OneTapeRegular** (logic/computability). [43] with digit input: Hennie–Trakhtenbrot; the base-k digit language is regular iff c is k-automatic; P1 ⟺ no fast one-tape deciders from both the base-2 and base-3 digits. `problem1_iff_no_fast_digit_deciders`, `isRegular_digitLang_iff`
- **UniformMorphic** (automata). [46], uniform case, by Cobham's little theorem: c is not both 2- and 3-uniformly morphic, nor a- and b-uniformly morphic for any multiplicatively independent a, b. `problem1_iff_not_uniformMorphic_two_three`, `problem1_iff_not_uniformMorphic`, `isAutomatic_iff_isUniformMorphic`
- **MeromorphicExtension** (analysis). [41], disk form: Σ c(t)zᵗ extends meromorphically to no disk of radius > 1 (Cauchy's estimate). `problem1_iff_no_meromorphic_extension`, `problem1_iff_no_meromorphicOn`
- **RegularSequences** (automata). [42], k-regular form: a 0/1 sequence is k-regular over a field iff it is k-automatic; P1 ⟺ c not both 2- and 3-regular. `problem1_iff_not_regularSeq_two_three`, `isRegularSeq_iff_isAutomatic`, `problem1_of_not_regularSeq`
- **ProfiniteIntegers** (number theory). No tail of c extends to a continuous function on Ẑ (the inverse limit of ℤ/(k+1)!ℤ); a continuous Ẑ → Bool reads one coordinate. `problem1_iff_no_continuous_extension`, `exists_continuous_extension_iff`, `Zhat`
- **Genericity** (dynamics). No new form ([34] through the seed): P1 ⟺ the trace image of the seed's ω-limit set is infinite ⟺ some limit configuration has a non-periodic column; disjunctive traces are comeager. `problem1_iff_trace_omegaLimit_seed_infinite`, `problem1_iff_exists_omegaLimit_seed_not_periodic`
- **Computability** (logic/computability). c is primitive recursive; P1 is Π⁰₂, "∀T, P ∃t ≥ T, c(t+P+1) ≠ c(t)", ⟺ the first-defect search halts on every input; P2 is Π⁰₃. `problem1_iff_forall_exists_defect`, `problem1_iff_firstDefect_dom`, `problem2_iff_forall_exists_forall`
- **ApproximateRecurrence** (analysis). Over any normed field: P1 ⟺ every monic Q has ‖(Q(σ)c)(n)‖ ≥ 1/2 for infinitely many n ⟺ no monic Q has (Q(σ)c)(n) → 0. `problem1_iff_no_approx_recurrence`, `problem1_iff_not_tendsto_zero`
- **Szego** (analysis). [41]: Σ c(t)zᵗ continues analytically across no arc of the unit circle (Szegő's theorem for 0/1 sequences). `problem1_iff_natural_boundary`, `eventuallyPeriodic_iff_continuation`, `eventuallyPeriodic_of_continuation`
- **Symmetry** (dynamics). The same question for rule 86 (black seed), for rules 135 and 149 (white seed), and for the complemented column. `problem1_iff_rule86`, `problem1_iff_rule135`, `problem1_iff_rule149`
- **Basic** (definitions). Shared definitions, the center column `c` and `EventuallyPeriodic`: P1 ⟺ c is not eventually periodic. `problem1_iff_not_eventuallyPeriodic`

### Sufficient for Problem 1 (one way) (8)

- **FrozenBoundary** (dynamics). No new form: the frozen-boundary conjecture (8 edge-rule steps). On genuine boundaries Φ, b, a it is ⟺ FinConf; no unbounded-orbit readout is eventually constant; no two adjacent readouts are both EP. `genuineFrozen_iff_finConfRows`, `not_adjacent_readouts` (implication: `AutomatonGroup.problem1_of_frozenBoundaryConjecture`)
- **Transcendence** (algebra). Sufficient only: Σ c(t)Xᵗ transcendental over K(X) for some field K, e.g. ℚ (converse over ℚ in AlgebraicDFinite), or over F₂(X) or F₃(X). `problem1_of_transcendental`, `problem1_of_transcendental_F2_or_F3`
- **NaturalBoundary** (analysis). Sufficient direction of [41]: if Σ c(t)zᵗ continues analytically across no arc of the unit circle, P1 holds (EP gives Q(z)/(1 − z^P)). `problem1_of_natural_boundary`, `exists_continuation`, `mul_genFun_eq`
- **StrongerStatements** (various). Sufficient: the CATALOG §4 statements (unbounded runs, positive Besicovitch distance, positive entropy, normal, x₂ transcendental, not morphic, …); one equivalence, μ(x₂) ≥ 2 (Dirichlet). `problem1_of_unbounded_runs`, `problem1_of_isNormal`, `problem1_of_far_from_periodic`, `problem1_iff_irrExponentGE`
- **PresburgerExpansion** (logic/computability). Sufficient (§4, undecidability rung): if multiplication is first-order definable in (ℕ, 0, 1, +, S), S the black times, P1 holds; disjunctive c ⟹ multiplication definable. `problem1_of_mul_definable`, `isSemilinearSet_of_definable`, `mul_definable_of_center_disjunctive`
- **BoundedRemainder** (probability). Sufficient: N(n) not αn + O(1) for any α; or P2 with N(n) − n/2 unbounded; or N(n) − n/2 unbounded above and below. Unpredictability at error rate 1/2 ⟹ P1 and P2. `problem1_of_unbounded_remainder`, `problem1_of_oscillating_discrepancy`, `problem2_of_unpredictable_half`
- **IrrationalityExponent** (number theory). No new form (§4). μ(x₂) = 2 (x₂ irrational, p-Liouville for no p > 2) implies P1 and holds almost surely (Khinchin). `problem1_of_exponentTwo`, `ae_exponentTwo_trace`, `ae_not_liouvilleWith`
- **Substitutive** (automata). [46] stated. Sufficient for integer bases: c not both a- and b-substitutive for some a, b ≥ 2 ⟹ P1; EP ⟹ k-substitutive. `problem1_of_not_substitutive`, `problem1_of_not_substitutive_two_three`, `isSubstitutive_of_eventuallyPeriodic`

### Problem 2 (6)

- **BlackTimes** (analysis). P2 ⟺ the k-th black cell occurs at time 2k + o(k) ⟺ the mean gap → 2; for L > 0, density L ⟺ k-th occurrence at k/L + o(k). `problem2_iff_trueTime`, `problem2_iff_mean_gap`, `halfDensity_iff_trueTime`
- **CesaroMeans** (analysis). P2 ⟺ the Cesàro means (C, k) of c tend to 1/2, for every k ≥ 1 (Toeplitz; Abel mean; Hardy–Littlewood–Karamata back to (C, 1)). `problem2_iff_cesaroMean`, `halfDensity_iff_cesaroMean`, `tendsto_weighted`
- **EmpiricalMeasures** (ergodic theory). P2 ⟺ every limit point of (δ_c + ⋯ + δ_{σᴺc})/(N + 1) gives cylinder [1] mass 1/2; normal ⟺ fair-coin generic; a non-atomic limit point ⟹ P1. `problem2_iff_mapClusterPt`, `isNormal_iff_tendsto_empirical`, `problem1_of_nonatomic_mapClusterPt`
- **HolderMeans** (analysis). P2 ⟺ the iterated Cesàro (Hölder) means of order k of c tend to 1/2, for every k ≥ 1 (Hardy's Tauberian theorem). `problem2_iff_holder`, `halfDensity_iff_holder`, `tendsto_of_tendsto_mean`
- **ProblemTwo** (analysis). P2 ⟺ black proportion → 1/2 ⟺ (1 − x)Σ c(t)xᵗ → 1/2 as x → 1⁻ ⟺ x₂ simply normal in base 2; normal ⟹ P2; density 1/2 on every AP ⟹ P1. `problem2_iff_tendsto`, `problem2_iff_abel`, `problem2_iff_simplyNormal`, `problem1_of_density_on_progressions`
- **P2Scales** (analysis). P2 ⟺ one nearly geometric sequence of nearly balanced scales ⟺ a first-passage lower bound. Sufficient: the frontier gap/accuracy form, or exact returns at nearly geometric scales. `problem2_iff_singleSequence`, `problem2_iff_firstPassage`, `problem2_of_epsGaps`, `problem2_of_exactReturns`

### Problem 3 (1)

- **ProblemThree** (logic/computability). Problem 3 (one-tape TM, binary n as input; no machine computes c(n) in time O(n), verbally o(n)) ⟹ c not 2-automatic ⟹ P1; so does the kit's `Problem3Robust`. `problem1_of_problem3`, `problem1_of_problem3Verbal`, `problem1_of_problem3Robust`

### Supporting results (no new form) (44)

- **TFunctionCycles** (algebra). No new form. Klimov–Shamir cycles of invertible T-functions mod 2ⁿ: the cycle length doubles at level i iff ψᵢ has odd parity around the cycle; exact return times of Φ's diagonals; diagonal readouts. `per_eq_two_pow_iff`, `Phi_cycle`, `exists_diagonal_prefix`
- **OrbitSignalizer** (dynamics). No new form. Exact top-bit growth distinguishes least-return section maps; unbounded prefix periods give infinitely many. This rules out finite exact-map closure, "not a property-preserving quotient or P1". `period_is_least`, `orbitSignalizer_infinite`
- **PositiveAutomaton** (automata). No new form. Positive words in the three finite-word Rule 30 states form a free monoid (Silva–Steinberg reset); distinct n-factor words differ on an input of exactly 2n bits. `positive_word_freeness`, `Bounds.faithful_at_twice_length`
- **FrozenBoundaryPeriodTwo** (dynamics). No new form. Period-2 case of the frozen-boundary conjecture: steps are triangular (exact death); `Q01` implies period 2 for all 8 steps; for Φ the period-2 question is exactly `CQ01`. `frozenBoundary_period_two_of_Q01`, `alternationFree_white_iff_CQ01`
- **FrozenBoundaryCore** (dynamics). No new form. The frozen-boundary conjecture = FinConf plus a core: the white-blinking edge of (1,0,1) and step (1,1,1), boundaries switching between (Φ, b) and (Φ, a, a, b). `frozenBoundaryConjecture_iff_core`, `step_101_two_steps`, `step_111_four_steps`
- **Lyndon** (combinatorics on words). No new form. Ehrenfeucht–Silberger: an infinite word over a finite ordered alphabet whose long factors are all bordered is EP (converse of [51]); Lyndon words are unbordered. `eventuallyPeriodic_of_bordered`, `IsLyndon.not_bordered`, `IsLyndon.append`
- **GoldenPowers** (combinatorics on words). No new form. Mignosi–Restivo–Salemi: an infinite word is EP iff every long enough prefix ends with a repetition of exponent ≥ φ² (converse of [47]). `eventuallyPeriodic_of_gp`, `first_lt`, `period_until`, `gp_sub`
- **Strassmann** (number theory). No new form. Strassmann: a nonzero series over ℚ_p with coefficients → 0 has finitely many zeros in the closed unit ball, at most the last index of a largest-norm coefficient. `strassmann`, `exists_zeros_subset`, `psum_sub_psum`
- **OrderDefinable** (logic/computability). No new form; a proved weaker statement (§5). The black times are not first-order definable in (ℕ, ≤), even with parameters (Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé). `not_definable_order`, `eventually_const_of_definable`
- **AlgebraicDegree** (algebra). No new form. The center cell after t ≥ 2 steps has ANF degree exactly 2t − 1 over 𝔽₂, top monomial x_{2−t}⋯x_t (t ≥ 3), x₀-coefficient c(t); balanced; [28] via `problem1_iff_no_feedback_degreeLE`. `isGreatest_card_coef_center`, `card_trace`
- **RightHalfReturns** (dynamics). No new form. Kopra Thm 4.5: from any configuration with a leftmost black cell, row t's right half equals row 0's for only finitely many t. `finite_returns`, `eventuallyPeriodic_of_return`, `periodic_rows`
- **Tauberian** (analysis). No new form. Hardy–Littlewood–Karamata: aₙ ≥ 0 and (1 − x)Σ aₙxⁿ → L as x → 1⁻ ⟹ (a₀ + ⋯ + a_{N−1})/N → L; also the Abelian direction for bounded sequences. `tendsto_cesaro_of_tendsto_abel`, `tendsto_abel_of_tendsto_cesaro`
- **BuchiConverse** (logic/computability). No new form. Converse of BuchiArithmetic (Büchi–Bruyère): k-automatic sets are definable in (ℕ, 0, 1, +, V_k); black times not (ℕ, +, V_k)-definable iff c not k-automatic. `definable_iff_isAutomatic`, `not_definable_iff_not_isAutomatic`
- **Odometer** (dynamics). No new form. In the right-edge frame rule 30 is the bijective isometry G(y)_j = y_j ⊕ (y_{j−1} ∨ y_{j−2}); ψ_a embeds ℤ₂ onto the orbit closure, conjugating α ↦ α + 1 to G. `isClosedEmbedding_ψ`, `ψ_add_one`, `G_bijective`
- **CenterFormulas** (algebra). No new form. Over 𝔽₂: c(t) = Σ_{t ≤ s < K}[cell(s, s−t+1) ∨ cell(s, s−t+2)] for any period K ≥ t of diagonal t; Duhamel: rule 30 = rule 150 + x_p x_{p+1}. `toF_center_eq_sum`, `duhamel`, `center_duhamel`
- **TwoAdicPeriods** (number theory). No new form. The weaker "no eventual period p^k" (§5), every prime p ⟺ no tail extends continuously to ℤ_p ⟺ the 𝔽_p Mahler coefficients of no tail vanish eventually. `noPrimePowPeriod_iff_not_continuous`, `noPrimePowPeriod_iff_fwdDiff`
- **OrbitFrequencies** (ergodic theory). No new form. For almost every configuration, every pattern on [−n, n] appears in the rows with frequency 2^−(2n+1), also along progressions of times. `ae_orbit_frequency`, `ae_orbit_frequency_progression`, `ae_tendsto_orbit_empirical`
- **QueryComplexity** (logic/computability). No new form (§6.2). A depth-d decision tree has 𝔽₂-degree ≤ d, so computing the center cell after t ≥ 2 steps needs ≥ 2t − 1 queries; depth 2t + 1 suffices. `le_depth_of_eval_eq`, `exists_depth_eq`
- **FiniteRings** (dynamics). No new form (§6.3). A ring of n cells is n-periodic rule 30; from one black cell its center equals c(t) for t < n, and the light cone agrees while 2t < n. `ringSeed`, `evol_ringSeed_eq_center`, `evol_ringSeed_eq_cell`
- **Preimages** (dynamics). No new form. At most 3 preimages (Hedlund's bound is 4); eventually white ⟹ exactly 2, eventually black ⟹ 3; pre-injective; not positively expansive; 010 arbitrarily far right ⟹ unique preimage. `card_le_three`, `exists_card_eq_three`, `not_positivelyExpansive`
- **RandomConfigurations** (probability). No new form. The center trace of a fair-coin configuration is fair-coin; almost surely normal, density 1/2, not EP (Borel); independent of the right half; CLT and Hoeffding. `measurePreserving_trace`, `ae_isNormal_trace`, `traceRightHalf`
- **Fluctuations** (probability). No new form. Almost surely, for every K, N(n) exceeds n/2 + K√n and falls below n/2 − K√n infinitely often; N(n) = n/2 infinitely often; within √(2n log log n) eventually. `ae_frequently_balanced_trace`, `ae_oscillating_discrepancy_trace`
- **Mixing** (ergodic theory). No new form. Rule 30 preserves the fair coin, is mixing of all orders and ergodic; almost surely a unique preimage; entropy between log 2 and log 3; lines of velocity ≠ 1 almost surely normal. `measurePreserving_evol`, `mixing_all_orders`, `ergodic_evol_one`, `ae_isNormal_lines`
- **Invertibility** (ergodic theory). No new form. Rule 30 is an automorphism of the fair-coin measure mod null sets, with a measurable inverse G; the two-sided center trace is i.i.d. fair coins; the Bernoulli shift is a factor. `exists_measurePreserving_inverse`, `measurePreserving_twoSidedTrace`
- **PeriodicPoints** (dynamics). No new form. F^k x = σ^d x with 1 − k ≤ d ≤ k ⟹ spatially periodic with period (4^k)!; at most 4^k such x; exactly three fixed points. `recurs_add_factorial`, `ncard_recurs_le`, `evol_one_eq_self_iff`
- **Autocorrelation** (probability). No new form. A normal sequence has disagreement frequency 1/2 at every lag τ ≥ 1 and differs from every periodic sequence at ≥ 1/4 of times; so almost surely for c. `tendsto_disagreements_of_isNormal`, `far_from_periodic_of_isNormal`, `ae_far_from_periodic_trace`
- **Typicality** (probability). No new form. Almost surely c meets eighteen §4 statements; the defect bound fails with probability ≥ 2⁻⁵; H_m ≠ 0 for all m ≥ 9 with probability ≥ 2⁻⁹. `ae_strongerStatements_trace`, `measure_not_defectBound_trace`, `measure_hankel_det_eq_zero_trace`
- **LinearComplexity** (probability). No new form (§4). Niederreiter: almost every fair-coin sequence has abs(2Lₙ − n) ≤ 2⌊log₂ n⌋ + 2 eventually, so Lₙ/n → 1/2; also the center column of almost every configuration. `ae_eventually_linComplexity`, `ae_tendsto_linComplexity_trace`
- **LongestRuns** (probability). No new form ([29]). Erdős–Rényi: almost surely the longest run of each colour among the first n cells has length ⌊log₂ n⌋(1 + o(1)). `ae_tendsto_longestRun`, `ae_tendsto_longestRun_trace`, `ae_eventually_longestRun`
- **ReturnTimes** (probability). No new form (§6.3). Wyner–Ziv: almost surely 2^n/(n + 1)² < R_n ≤ n(n + 1)² 2^n eventually, so (log₂ R_n)/n → 1. `ae_eventually_returnTime`, `ae_tendsto_logb_returnTime_trace`
- **IteratedLogarithm** (probability). No new form. Khinchin LIL: almost surely W(n) = 2N(n) − n has limsup/liminf W(n)/√(2n log log n) = ±1 with limit points [−1, 1]; comeager: limsup/liminf W(n)/n = ±1. `ae_limsup_liminf_walk_trace`, `ae_clusterPt_walk_trace`, `residual_limsup_liminf_walk_div_trace`
- **Circuits** (logic/computability). No new form (§4, P3 relatives). Almost surely, for large k, no circuit with ≤ 2ᵏ/(8k) binary gates computes t ↦ c(t), t < 2ᵏ, from the k digits of t (Shannon). `ae_circuit_lower_bound_trace`, `ae_eventually_no_small_circuit`
- **LargeDeviations** (probability). No new form. Cramér: for a random configuration and 1/2 ≤ a < 1, (1/n) log P(N(n) ≥ an) → H(a) − log 2, H the binary entropy. `tendsto_log_measureReal_trace`, `card_le_chernoff`
- **ErdosRenyi** (probability). No new form. For 1/2 < α < 1, almost surely the largest black count in windows of length ⌊log n/(log 2 − H(α))⌋ among the first n cells, divided by the length, → α. `ae_tendsto_maxWindow_trace`, `ae_tendsto_maxWindow`
- **Lines** (probability). No new form. Almost surely, along every rational-velocity line p/q ≠ 1 at once: LIL, longest runs, return times, linear complexity, Erdős–Rényi, natural boundary, max-order complexity 2 log₂ n + o(log n). `ae_lil_lines`, `ae_circleIsNaturalBoundary_lines`, `Mixing.ae_lines_of_ae`
- **RandomNaturalBoundary** (analysis). The [41] sufficient condition holds almost surely: Σ c(t)zᵗ has the unit circle as natural boundary (Steinhaus, Paley–Zygmund). `ae_circleIsNaturalBoundary_trace`, `problem1_of_circleIsNaturalBoundary`
- **LocalLimit** (probability). No new form. de Moivre–Laplace: if (kₙ − n/2)/√n → x then √n C(n, kₙ)/2ⁿ → √(2/π)e^(−2x²); first 2n cells half black with probability (1 + o(1))/√(πn). `tendsto_sqrt_mul_measureReal_trace`, `tendsto_sqrt_mul_choose_div`
- **MaxOrderComplexity** (probability). No new form ([28]). Almost surely the maximum-order complexity M_n of c is 2 log₂ n (1 + o(1)), and so along every line. `ae_tendsto_maxOrderComplexity_trace`, `ae_tendsto_maxOrderComplexity`
- **SzegoPolynomial** (analysis). Toward [41]. For 0 < τ < π/2 there are ρ₁ < 1 < ρ₂ and q < 1 such that for every D some monic polynomial is ≤ 2qᴰ on a notched annulus (Chebyshev). `exists_notch_poly`, `norm_eval_notchPoly_le`, `refined_bound`
- **SzegoContour** (analysis). Szegő's analytic step: Σ aₙzⁿ with ‖aₙ‖ ≤ 1 continuing to a disk around 1 ⟹ for every ε > 0 some monic W has ‖Σⱼ wⱼ a(n+j)‖ < ε for every n. `exists_approx_recurrence`, `sector_integral_eq`
- **PerronFrobenius** (algebra). Toward [46]. Perron–Frobenius for primitive real matrices: eigenvalue r > 0 with a positive eigenvector; Aʲ/rʲ → v wᵀ; every other eigenvalue has modulus < r. `exists_eigenvector`, `tendsto_pow_div`, `norm_lt_of_mulVec_eq`
- **LinearRecurrence** (combinatorics on words). Toward [46]. Primitive substitutive sequences are linearly recurrent: u occurs in every interval of L·abs(u); if not EP, occurrences p < p + d give abs(u) < L d. `isLinearlyRecurrent_of_isPrimitive`, `length_lt_of_occursAt`
- **TypicalConditions** (probability). No new form. The sufficient conditions outside §4 hold almost surely; almost surely all three Prize problems hold; generically Problems 1 and 3 hold and Problem 2 fails. `ae_sufficientConditions_trace`, `ae_prizeProblems_trace`, `residual_prizeProblems_trace`
- **LimitPoints** (dynamics). No new form. Kopra: the right halves of the rows from the seed, or from any configuration with a leftmost black cell, have infinitely many limit points in {0,1}^ℕ (Jen). `infinite_limitPoints_cell`, `infinite_limitPoints_evol`, `exists_periodic_window`
